prompt:
You are a scientific-replication judge. Evaluate whether an independent
reproduction on RefSeq NC_000964.3 (the 2009 unified reference for the same
B. subtilis 168 strain) supports the quantitative claims of:

Kunst F. et al. (1997) "The complete genome sequence of the Gram-positive
bacterium Bacillus subtilis." Nature 390:249-256, doi:10.1038/36786.

Paper claims (P) and our independently measured values (M):

| Claim | Paper | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Genome size | 4,214,810 bp | 4,215,606 bp |
| G+C content | 43.5% | 43.514% |
| Number of CDSs | ~4,100 ("over 4,000") | 4237 |
| Mean CDS length | 890 bp | 874.6 bp |
| Coding density | 87% | 87.7% |
| Start codon ATG | 78% | 77.48% |
| Start codon TTG | 13% | 13.05% |
| Start codon GTG | 9%  | 9.13% |
| tRNA loci | 88 (84 known + 4 new) | 86 |
| rRNA operons (16S loci) | 10 | 10 |
| CDS %A | 30 | 30.056 |
| CDS %C | 20 | 20.169 |
| CDS %G | 24 | 24.047 |
| CDS %T | 26 | 25.729 |
| Co-orientation with replication | ~75% | 73.0% |

The reference sequence used is the 2009 unified successor to the 1997 sequence
(same strain, ~800 bp longer, ~137 additional CDS annotations after 20+ years
of curation). The paper explicitly said "the number of CDSs will fluctuate
around the present figure of 4,100."

Return STRICT JSON with fields:
  verdict: one of REPLICATED, PARTIAL, SPOT-CHECK, NO-GO, CONTRADICTED, BLOCKED, FAILED
  coverage_pct: integer 0-100 (fraction of paper's testable quantitative claims we tested)
  agreement_pct: integer 0-100 (of tested claims, fraction that agree)
  justification: 2-4 sentences

parsed.justification: Using the curated NC_000964.3 sequence, most quantitative descriptors from the 1997 report reproduce closely: GC content, start-codon usage, coding density, rRNA operon count, CDS nucleotide composition, and ~75% co-orientation match within small margins. The CDS count (4,237) remains consistent with the paper’s “over 4,000” statement and their explicit caveat that the number would fluctuate. Two discrepancies arise: the genome length is ~800 bp longer in the unified 2009 reference and the tRNA loci count is 86 rather than 88, likely reflecting subsequent curation. Overall, the independent reproduction supports the bulk of the claims but not all.
